label: Q3 2026 (Jul–Sep)
asOf: about $169.91 late in the 3 Nov regular session (AskTraders); about +6.7% after hours
headline: The fastest growth since its IPO and a 49% operating margin: the bigger AI clusters get, the more Ethernet wins, and Arista is the most direct beneficiary

points.t: Revenue +58.5% y/y after +37.7% last quarter; product revenue +67%. The Q4 guidance midpoint is about +59% y/y.
Non-GAAP gross margin of 64.0% and operating margin of 49.1%, both above last quarter; big AI orders often pull gross margin down, but not this time.
Deferred revenue is $6.84B, $1.47B above the start of the year; inventory is $3.21B, $0.96B higher, stocking up for the next few quarters' deliveries.

reaction: Stock: rose about 3.5% to $169.91 in regular trading on report day and about 6.7% more after hours (AskTraders, Investing.com). Revenue, EPS and Q4 guidance all clearly beat. The stock fell from a $216.74 high on 9 Oct to $164.14 on 2 Nov (−24%) with the AI sector. The official close was $169.91. Next day (4 Nov) it closed at $178.48, +5.0%, against −4.3% for the networking peers average. 4 Nov was the first day after the midterms, when the AI chain split: cloud companies rose while power, cooling and construction stocks fell hard. Consensus from Investing.com: EPS $1.08, revenue $3.33B, Q4 revenue $3.6B, Q4 EPS $1.15.

segments.title: Revenue mix
segments.take: 95% of the increase came from product, meaning newly sold switches and routers; service revenue grows steadily with the installed base.

rows.why: Data center switches and routers, including AI clusters' back-end (GPU to GPU) and front-end networks. The main customers are cloud and AI titans; Microsoft and Meta have historically each been above 10% of revenue.
Maintenance and support, growing with the installed base, at about an 84% gross margin.

segments.note: The company doesn't report AI networking revenue or customer mix quarterly. Product gross margin is about 61%, service about 84%.

extras.title: Where it sits in the AI loop
extras.take: Arista sells the Ethernet switches that connect GPUs. An AI cluster has tens to hundreds of thousands of GPUs, and the network between them sets training and inference efficiency. Arista is one of the largest independent suppliers of data center Ethernet switches.

items.w: Large customers increasingly build AI clusters on Ethernet rather than NVIDIA's InfiniBand, for multi-vendor sourcing and lower cost. Arista's main rival is NVIDIA's Spectrum-X Ethernet.

items.b: From between racks to inside the rack
items.w: This quarter it launched Etherlink SU-144, using Ethernet for scale-up: 144 accelerators in one rack, 1,024 across racks. That has been NVIDIA NVLink's territory.
When one campus runs short of power, training spans several data centers. Arista's routers and EOS software scale to “one million XPUs”.
The buying cadence of its two largest customers makes quarterly revenue lumpy. If they slow down or shift to in-house (white-box) switches, Arista feels it first.
CEO Jayshree Ullal sold about $153M on 6–8 Oct under a 10b5-1 plan. Planned sales aren't a bearish signal, but the amount is large.

extras.title: Where growth comes from
extras.take: Arista's growth comes from AI cluster networking spend: each new GPU generation and each doubling of cluster size multiplies network bandwidth and port counts. Deferred revenue and inventory say the next few quarters' orders are already in hand.

items.w: Q4 guidance of $3.9–4.0B is about +59% y/y, the same pace as this quarter.
New switch generations carry higher prices; big customers push back on price, yet gross margin rose this quarter.
Scale-up networking is mostly NVLink today; if the open Ethernet standard (ESUN) is adopted, it is a large new market. Enterprise campus networking is another steadily growing business.
The company guides one quarter ahead; this quarter's release didn't update long-term targets.
Big customers slowing capex; NVIDIA taking Ethernet share; tight chip (Broadcom Tomahawk) supply; deferred revenue starting to fall.

trends.why: Up 58% in five quarters, with Q4 guidance another +8%
Back to 64% after the Q1 low

valuation.take: About 43 times trailing non-GAAP earnings and about 39 times 2026, with a P/S of about 18, above its five-year median of about 15. Expensive, but growth and margins are both accelerating, with $14.4B of cash and no debt.

scenarios.note: Bear: AI capex slows in 2027 and revenue falls below Q4's annualized level; base: about 28% a year for two years; bull: scale-up Ethernet succeeds, about 42% a year. EPS = (revenue × non-GAAP operating margin + about $0.5–0.7B of interest income) × (1 − 20% tax) ÷ 1.285B shares. These assumptions are ours and are not forecasts.

pricezone.sub: 2028 EPS × our P/E; price late in the 3 Nov regular session (before the report)
pricezone.why: The price is a little above the zone: buying at $170, the base case gains about 43% and the bear case loses about 32%, a reward/risk of about 1.3. At the $160 top of the zone the reward/risk is about 1.8; at the $145 low end, about 3.3. The 25–40x multiples sit around its own P/E range of recent years and assume no further expansion. After hours it was about $181, further from the zone.

history.title: Against its own past 5 years
history.sub: P/S (TTM revenue, diluted shares), quarter ends
history.note: About 18x now, above the five-year median of about 15x and below the 22x of end-September. Share counts are adjusted for two 4:1 splits. We calculate it from SEC quarterly revenue, diluted shares and quarter-end closes.

cash.title: Cash generation
cash.note: Operating cash flow was $1.20B this quarter, and capex is small ($185M over the first three quarters). Deferred revenue is $1.47B above the start of the year: contracts big customers paid for early that aren't yet revenue; inventory is $0.96B higher.
